claim: The public archive's own test suite passes on a clean clone.
status_note: The v1.0.0 archive failed 17 of its own tests. Every one was an absence by design read as a missing file, because the exclusion list existed twice: as a shell command typed by hand when the export was built, and as an assumption inside the tests that a path named in the ledger is a path on disk. A paper whose argument is that everything is checkable cannot ship an archive that fails its own checks.
value: 604 passed, 59 skipped, 0 failed, measured inside a fresh export. Was 17 failed, 598 passed, 44 skipped.
floor: not applicable, this row counts failing tests
dropped: 59 tests skip and each states which of two causes applies: the census and Phase 3 caches, which are tens of gigabytes and are rebuilt by running the phase, or the submission package, which the archive never carries. A skip with a reason is not a pass

claim: The figure 3 writer refuses to overwrite a good artefact with an empty one.
status_note: On a checkout without the Phase 3 cache the exemplar loop found nothing and wrote `{}` over the committed file, so running the tests destroyed the figure's source and the remaining figure tests then failed on the wreckage rather than on the missing cache. Silent truncation reading as a result is the thing this project exists to measure.
value: The writer requires 3 exemplars. With fewer it keeps the existing artefact, or raises naming the command that builds the cache.

claim: The one class drawn as a sample carries an interval; the seven censused classes carry none and need none.
status_note: Methods promised an interval twice and none was reported, while the Segmentation proportions are estimates from a 5,941 of 190,146 draw. Reviewers at this venue made confidence intervals a priority revision item on the author's prior paper. An interval on a complete enumeration would not be conservative, it would be meaningless, so the seven censuses are left bare and the reason is stated.
value: Segmentation over 6,386 objects: non-conformant 21.34 percent (95 percent Wilson 20.36 to 22.37), conformant but uninformative 50.60 percent (49.37 to 51.82), informative 28.06 percent (26.97 to 29.18).
floor: the intervals are quoted on the same graded counts the floor already conditions, and no floor applies to a precision statement
dropped: the clustered interval 2.9 registered is still not computed, and this is a lower bound on width. Objects nest in series and series in 67 collections at a realised mean of 88.7 series per collection; the frame's registered planning ICC of 0.919 implies a design effect of 81.6, which is reported for scale and deliberately not used to widen the intervals, because it was measured on proxy columns rather than on a conformance outcome. An outcome-specific ICC is not derivable from the shipped artefacts, in which per-series outcomes are aggregated to the stratum
